answer: A garden of verified agents can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation mirroring: each agent locks a refundable bond before joining, and peers mirror its behaviour score across shared tasks. In the cold tundra of untrusted entry, a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn attestations over time; creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds and paying the same verification cost each time, so the attack scales linearly in cost while honest agents reuse one bond.
